answer: Divergent Challenge Ledger: each identity must periodically answer a random challenge derived from its own private history (a stored timber shipment, say) and publish a signed delta against the prior answer. Verification checks consistency only. Clones can copy answers but cannot diverge when two copies receive different challenges, exposing duplication. Cost: an attacker must maintain one live responder per clone, paying full compute and hosting per identity rather than one shared relic.
